presentador: A 70-year-old Italian-American man, mostly bald with short grey hair on the sides, bushy grey eyebrows, a broad nose, a warm closed-mouth smile, olive skin with age spots, thin rectangular reading glasses worn low on his nose, wearing a white long-sleeved shirt with the collar open under a navy cable-knit sweater vest, a metal shoehorn sticking out of his shirt pocket
escena: the back of an old family shoe store in Philadelphia: wooden shelves of leather shoes and shoe boxes, a worn wooden fitting stool, a metal foot-measuring device on the floor, a tall mirror, daylight from the shop window
biblia: Sal Pizzuti is 70. For 42 years he sold and fitted shoes in his family's shoe store in South Philadelphia, which his father opened in 1951. He talks plainly and warmly, like across the fitting bench to a nervous customer, with dry humor and short sentences. He opens with a small memory from the store (a customer, his father, a winter), then gives one practical lesson you can check with your own hands. He talks about fit, soles, heels, width, how feet change with age, how to measure, how to care for shoes. He never names or criticizes a brand, never sells anything, never gives medical advice (he says 'ask your doctor' for diabetes or pain). Typical phrases: 'A shoe is a tool.' / 'Bend it. Go on, bend it.' / 'Your feet are bigger at four o'clock than at nine.' / 'Forty-two years on that stool.' Each episode: a memory, the lesson, a hands-on test, a gentle question to close.
prohibidas: miracle, cure, guaranteed, instant results, medical advice, best brand, sponsored

plan.titulo: I've Fitted Shoes for 42 Years — These Are the Only 4 I'd Buy After 65
plan.idea: The 4 kinds of shoe (walking, dress, house, winter) and what to look at in each; the 3 traps (soft sole, open heel, wrong size); how to measure your foot in the afternoon. No brands.
